cohort: The study participants were antenatal women presenting with reduced fetal movements during term pregnancy.
finding: Reduced fetal movements (RFM) are connected with severe perinatal hazards, including NICU admissions, intrauterine fetal demise, and low birth weight, necessitating close observation and prompt intervention.
mod_finding: Reduced fetal movements are associated with higher rates of caesarean section delivery.
cross-section timing: The study evaluated antenatal women presenting with reduced fetal movements in term pregnancy, assessing maternal and fetal outcomes around the time of delivery.
birth_weight: 20% of the neonates experienced low birth weight.
gest_age: Most (75.3%) of the deliveries occurred between 37-40 weeks of gestation.
